newsitem.title: USA: MFS/UUNET plans Internet over xDSL lines.
newsitem.headline: MFS/UUNET plans Internet over xDSL lines.

text.p: MFS Communications Co Inc and its UUNET Technologies unit said Monday they planned to offer the first commercial service capable of providing high-speed Internet access over traditional telephone lines.
MFS said its new unswitched "xDSL," or Digital Subscriber Line, service will be available early in the first quarter of 1997 in selected U.S. markets and eventually nationwide.
The service was jointly developed with Ascend Communications Inc.
MFS is in the process of being acquired by WorldCom Inc.
The service, which has already completed testing, will be priced to attract small- and mid-size businesses, MFS said.
In providing what is a direct, dedicated line to the Internet, the new service offers advantages not currently available through other technologies, the company said.

The service bypasses conventional telephone network switches, allowing access to the Internet at 128 kilobits per second, or four times faster than the 28.8 kilobit modems now used by most computer users to connect to the Internet.
The service should help reduce the level of congestion on traditional switched telephone networks caused by Internet data traffic.
